conviction_note: Via's own documents point to a small beat and a fourth FY raise. Q1 and Q2 each beat the top of the quarterly revenue guide by 1.3-2.9%, and Q3 consensus of $137.9m sits on the guide midpoint. But this name sold two of its last three guide beats at the event (-16.6%, -7.5%, +0.9%). It has also run about 75% since the spring and 47% since the last print, while 11.5% of the float is short. So the fundamental lean (print_vs_bar +1.5%) does not carry through to a reaction lean. p_up stays 50 on a wide move (abs 11%, the name's median reaction; the options chain is unusable). The findings sum to -0.8 because the positioning and margin items slightly outweigh the beat pattern; both measurements are close to zero and do not conflict.
bar: Q3 2026 platform revenue guide $137.6-138.2m and adj. EBITDA guide -$4.5m to -$3.5m, from the company's Q2 release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001603015/000160301526000027/viaq226pressrelease.htm, 2026-08-06). Revenue consensus is about $137.9m, which is the guide midpoint, per Benzinga (https://www.benzinga.com/quote/VIA/earnings-forecasts) and the Earnings Whispers preview of 2026-11-02 (https://finviz.com/news/413691/vias-75-rally-sets-a-high-bar-as-school-launches-and-pipeline-face-their-test). Two sources agree, and both match the company guide. FY2026 guide is revenue $550-553m and adj. EBITDA -$12.5m to -$7.5m, with Q4 2026 adj. EBITDA > $0. FY26 revenue consensus is $551.74m (stockanalysis, updated 2026-11-04, https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/via/forecast/), on the guide midpoint. EPS consensus is disputed (-$0.07 Benzinga, -$0.03 TipRanks, -$0.23 Earnings Whispers), so no finding is sized on EPS.
positioning_check: Short interest is 6.67m shares at the 2026-10-15 FINRA settlement (Equibles, citing FINRA: https://equibles.com/stocks/via/short-interest), down 1.26m from the prior period. Days to cover are 11.0 on Equibles' volume basis and 7.41 on stockanalysis's (https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/via/statistics, page updated 2026-11-06). That is 11.53% of a 57.9m float. Borrow fee is about 0.8% (curvedtrading, https://curvedtrading.com/stocks/via/), so the short is moderately crowded but not hard to borrow. The options chain is unusable: ATM spread is 81% of mid, total open interest is 339 and put/call OI is 0.17. So there is no skew, and the baseline carries no priced direction. The tape: spot $36.99, +14.3% over 20 days, +177% off the 52-week low, -28% from the 52-week high. Earnings Whispers says the stock is near its post-earnings high ($36.91) after a roughly 75% rally, with bullish sentiment down to 22.4% from 36.1% before the last report.

findings.finding: Via has beaten the top of its own quarterly revenue guide two quarters running and raised the FY guide both times. Q1 2026 guide was $123.3-123.8m and actual was $127.4m (+$3.6m over the high end). Q2 guide was $132.5-134.0m and actual was $135.7m (+$1.7m). The FY guide went from $542.9-545.1m to $547-550m to $550-553m. Q3 consensus of $137.9m sits exactly on the $137.6-138.2m guide midpoint, so repeating the pattern means revenue of about $139.5-141m (+1-2% vs the bar) and a fourth FY raise to about $552-556m.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Beats over the top of the guide have not been paid at the event. Q4 2025 'surpassed guidance across all key metrics' and the stock fell 7.53% (2026-02-27). Q1 2026 beat the top of the guide by 2.9% and raised the FY guide, and the stock fell 16.6% (2026-05-12). Q2 2026 beat by 1.3% and raised again; the stock rose 0.94% on the day (2026-08-06) and then drifted about +47%.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus sits on the guide midpoint, not above it, so the street has not modelled the beat cadence into the quarter, and FY consensus of $551.74m is the guide midpoint too. If the beat were priced, consensus would sit near the top of the range. But the Earnings Whispers preview names the beat-and-raise record outright, and the stock has run 75%, so the pattern is probably in the price even though it is not in the estimates.
findings.independence: The Q2 release shows the same pattern (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001603015/000160301526000027/viaq226pressrelease.htm), and the Q4 2025 release gives the original FY guide (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1603015/000160301526000002/viaq425pressrelease.htm). Both are company documents, so this is one company's track record rather than independent confirmation.

findings.finding: The held FY adj. EBITDA guide has almost no slack. YTD adj. EBITDA is Q1 -$5.8m plus Q2 -$3.4m, and with the Q3 guide midpoint of -$4.0m that comes to -$13.2m, already below the FY guide's low end of -$12.5m. Holding the FY range on 9 Nov therefore requires Q4 adj. EBITDA of at least +$0.7m, or +$3.2m to reach the FY midpoint. If Q3 prints at the bottom of its guide (-$4.5m), Q4 must reach +$1.2m. Q3 is also guided as a step back from Q2's -$3.4m, which management put down to seasonality and launch investments (school-year launches). So the line the stock is watching, first-ever positive Q4 EBITDA, rests on a Q4 swing of $4-8m from Q3.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The FY EBITDA guide has been held unchanged at -$12.5m to -$7.5m in all three releases of 2026 (Q4'25, Q1'26, Q2'26), so the line has never surprised. Q1's EBITDA beat its guide (-$5.8m vs -$7.25m to -$6.75m) and the stock still fell 16.6%.
findings.why_not_priced: Previews quote 'Q4 adj. EBITDA > $0' as a target but do not do the YTD walk showing that the FY guide's low end is already breached at the Q3 midpoint. If the market had priced the risk of a slip, a reaffirmed Q4 target would be a relief trade and the run-up would have stalled into the print. Neither has happened. This is arithmetic on company numbers, not a forecast of a miss: Q1 beat its EBITDA guide by about $1.2m, which is why the size is small.
findings.independence: The Q1 release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1603015/000160301526000013/viaq126pressrelease.htm) carries Q1 EBITDA. The Earnings Whispers preview of 2026-11-02 (https://finviz.com/news/413691/vias-75-rally-sets-a-high-bar-as-school-launches-and-pipeline-face-their-test) separately notes that some margin pullback is expected and that a sharp margin reversal would challenge the thesis. It shares the company documents as its source.

findings.finding: Rochester (MN) City Council awarded Via Transit Twin Cities the Rochester Public Transit operating contract on 2026-07-06: 64 months, more than $77.8m (about $1.2m a month), with operations starting 2026-09-01. That puts about one month (~$1.2m) in Q3 and a full quarter (~$3.6m) in Q4. The award came before the 2026-08-06 guide, so it should be inside both the Q3 and FY ranges. It is evidence of the 'full-network takeover' conversion that previews say investors are watching.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No release has broken out a single contract's contribution. Earlier large awards (TCATA, 2026-01-22; Mobile) were announced as press releases and are not separable from the print reactions.
findings.why_not_priced: Via issued no press release for Rochester; its IR list shows nothing between 2026-06-25 and 2026-10-06. So the award reached investors only through local TV, though it was public before the guide was set. It is mostly inside the guide, which is why it is sized near zero.
findings.independence: Previews mention a growth contract value above $700m, doubling year on year, and 114 customers above $1m (https://finviz.com/news/413691/vias-75-rally-sets-a-high-bar-as-school-launches-and-pipeline-face-their-test). Those figures come from company commentary, not from this contract.

findings.finding: Positioning into the print is stretched on the long side and crowded on the short side at once. The stock is up about 75% in a few months and about 47% since the 2026-08-06 print (a director bought at $24.74 on 2026-08-11; spot is $36.99), trades near its post-earnings high, and is +14.3% over 20 days, with consensus PT ($37.67, 10 analysts) now about 2% above spot. Against that, 6.67m shares (11.5% of float, 7-11 days to cover) are short. Earnings Whispers bullish sentiment fell from 36.1% to 22.4%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: After the Q1 run into May the print fell 16.6%. After the Q2 print, from a low base, the stock drifted up about 47%. The name has moved 7-17% on three of its four prints.
findings.why_not_priced: This is the price itself, so it is the bar rather than mispriced information. It is filed because a stock at the consensus price target with momentum holders can fall on a reaffirm (the preview says a reaffirmation 'could disappoint a stock priced for momentum'). The negative is cut for the 11.5%-of-float short with 7-11 days to cover, which gives a squeeze mechanism on a beat-and-raise.
findings.independence: Short interest is from https://equibles.com/stocks/via/short-interest and https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/via/statistics. The price target is from https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/via/forecast/. The director's purchase is in a Form 4: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1603015/000162828026056412/xslF345X06/wk-form4_1786573644.xml.

findings.finding: Director Nechemia Jacob Peres (Pitango) bought 10,080 shares in the open market on 2026-08-11 at a weighted $24.74 (about $250k). It was the only insider purchase in the window, and there have been no insider sales or Form 144s since July: EDGAR shows only this purchase, an RSU grant to the Chief Legal Officer (2026-08-18) and a Form 3.
findings.why_not_priced: It is public and three months old, and the stock is up about 50% since, so it is essentially priced. What it adds is the absence of insider selling into the rally, which an insider with a weak Q3 view could have done but did not.
findings.independence: The EDGAR submissions list (https://data.sec.gov/submissions/CIK0001603015.json) shows no other Form 4 sales or Form 144 since 2026-07-01.

findings.finding: Germany, the issue at the centre of the IPO class action, is still shrinking. Q2 2026 German revenue was $18.28m against $20.74m a year earlier (-12%), about 13% of revenue, in a quarter where the US grew 35% to $103.3m. A continued German decline is a drag of roughly 0.3-0.5 points on group growth. US growth of about 30% is what the guide already counts on, so net of the rest of the company the German line only bites if it accelerates down.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The 2026-05-12 print (-16.6%) is the class period's end date in the lawsuit, which cites trouble growing in Germany and a declining run-rate. That implies the German line has moved this stock before.
findings.why_not_priced: The geographic split sits in the 10-Q footnote, not the press release, and previews do not mention Germany. If it were priced, previews would treat German revenue as a watched line. It is a small segment, so the size is small.
findings.independence: The IPO class-action complaint summary (https://www.newsfilecorp.com/release/300816/ScottScott-Attorneys-at-Law-LLP-Files-Securities-Class-Action-Against-Via-Transportation-Inc.-VIA) names trouble growing in Germany. That is a separate party, but it is an allegation.

findings.finding: The 41% adjusted gross margin in Q2 2026 was partly lifted by one-time, non-subscription revenue that management said would fade, according to the Earnings Whispers preview of the call. The preview also cites a stronger Israeli shekel inflating R&D costs (the shekel hit a 33-year high of about 2.88-2.90 per dollar in May 2026). Both point to a softer Q3 gross margin and opex line, which management guided for.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Adjusted gross margin rose from 40% to 41% in Q2 2026, and the stock was flat on the day (+0.94%). There is no case of a margin miss.
findings.why_not_priced: It is in management commentary and in the Q3 EBITDA guide step-back, so it is largely inside the guide and expected. It is filed small because a gross-margin dip below 40% would undercut the operating-leverage story.
findings.independence: The shekel strength is reported by JNS (https://www.jns.org/news/israel-news/shekel-hits-33-year-high-against-dollar). That is a macro proxy and the company has not quantified it.

outside_window.finding: IPO securities class action, Garlesky v. Via Transportation, S.D.N.Y. No. 1:26-cv-04870, Securities Act §§11/12/15. The lead plaintiff deadline was 2026-08-10, and nothing in it is scheduled to resolve by 2026-11-10.
FY2027 guidance: FY27 revenue consensus is $674.6m (+22%) and EPS $0.39. Via issues its FY guide with the Q4 release in late February, so a first 2027 guide is not expected on 9 Nov.

searched_and_found_nothing: Via IR press-release feed (https://investors.ridewithvia.com/feed/PressRelease.svc/GetPressReleaseList?...year=2026): no release between 2026-08-06 and the 2026-10-06 date notice, so no contract, M&A or pre-announcement.
EDGAR submissions since 2026-07-01: no 8-K after 2026-08-06, no Form 144, no insider sales (https://data.sec.gov/submissions/CIK0001603015.json).
News search for a September-October 2026 catalyst behind the 47% post-print drift: nothing beyond generic 'beat and raise' commentary (Trefis, Earnings Whispers).
New Waymo-Via cities in 2026: nothing beyond Chandler (Sept 2025).
Problems with school transportation launches in the 2026-27 school year (late buses, district complaints): nothing found.
A 2026 federal government shutdown affecting FTA grants to transit agencies: nothing found for October 2026.
Contracts ending or lost in Germany: nothing found.
Independent ridership or app-download series for Via's agency services: not attempted beyond the above, because Via's revenue is agency contract revenue, not consumer usage.

rejected_candidates.detail: The litigation timeline runs past 2026-11-10; filed in outside_window at 0.

Remaining performance obligations of $318.3m at 2026-06-30, 45% to be recognised in the rest of 2026 (about $143m against about $288m of implied H2 revenue)
rejected_candidates.detail: Covers only about half of H2 revenue and says nothing beyond the guide. Merged into the beat-pattern and Rochester findings as context rather than counted as a separate fact.

baseline_tension: There is no skew to agree or disagree with because the chain is unusable. The company-level documents lean mildly toward a beat and raise, while the 75% rally, the 14% 20-day run-up and a history of selling beats lean against paying for it. The 11.5% short float cuts the other way, so the evidence offsets and p_up sits at 50.
lessons_applied: Lesson 1 (a verified fact is not a predicted reaction): cut the beat-and-raise finding from +1.0 to +0.6, because Via fell 16.6% and 7.5% on two of its three guide beats.
Lesson 7 (positioning): cut the stretched-positioning negative from -1.0 to -0.7 after confirming 11.5% of float short with 7-11 days to cover (Equibles, stockanalysis).
Lesson 9 (size a segment net of the company): cut the Germany finding from -0.3 to -0.2, because the US is 76% of revenue and grew 35%.
Lesson 8 / core 3b (hunters' sizes run small): raised abs_move_pct from 10 to 11, the name's own median reaction, since a FY raise is likely and the name moves 7-17% on most prints. p_up stays at 50.

Lesson 6 (verify the bar): the revenue bar is the company guide plus two agreeing estimates, so no cap. The EPS bar is disputed, so no finding rests on EPS. The sum is unchanged at -0.8 because the cuts offset.
